nodes.description: The metaphyseal/jaw fibro-osseous lesions of OGD can behave aggressively as recurrent central giant cell granulomas (CGCG). In a long-followed adult with molecularly characterized OGD whose maxillary CGCG recurred through repeated surgery and failed alendronate, switching to the anti-RANKL monoclonal antibody denosumab — which acts directly on the osteoclast-like giant cells of the lesion rather than indirectly on bone resorption — produced marked tumour regression. This is a single case, not a trial, and denosumab in a growing skeleton carries its own hazards (medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw, hypocalcaemia, atypical fracture, post-treatment rebound), so it is recorded here as an emerging lesion-directed option rather than standard care.

nodes.description: A subset of individuals with FGFR1-related OGD have elevated circulating FGF23 with consequent renal phosphate wasting and hypophosphatemia. FGF23 is produced chiefly by cells of the osteoblast/osteocyte lineage — the same lineage in which the activating FGFR1 allele is expressed — and acts on the proximal renal tubule to suppress phosphate reabsorption. This arm is biochemical rather than structural and is not part of the shared FGFR growth-plate/suture mechanism, so it is deliberately kept as a separate node with no `conforms_to` anchor: it is what makes OGD more than "Pfeiffer syndrome plus metaphyseal lesions".
